brief: Überarbeitung der vom Nutzer gewählten Gitarrenkomposition: Gesicht enger an Originalfotos orientiert, anschließend deutliche Reduktion von Details und Textur bei unveränderter zurückgenommener Tonlage.

steps.title: Gesicht und erste Vereinfachung
steps.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Task: revise the 2006 guitar portrait, correcting its facial likeness and reducing its excessive detail. One finished vertical 4:5 artwork.

REFERENCE PRIORITY, CRITICAL:
Images 1, 2 and 3 are ORIGINAL PHOTOGRAPHS OF JACKIE LEVEN IN 2006. They are the only authority for identity and facial anatomy. Image 1 is the clearest primary reference for his individual facial structure, with image 2 supporting his fuller face and hair; image 3 supports his eyes and expression. Ignore the photographs' colors, stage, microphone, lighting and overall composition.
Image 4 is the EDIT TARGET: its seated composition with a resting forearm and acoustic guitar has been approved, BUT ITS FACE IS WRONG AND ITS DETAIL IS EXCESSIVE. Do not preserve or perpetuate that invented facial structure. Treat image 4 only as a guide for overall body arrangement and guitar placement.
Image 5 is the APPROVED SERIES STYLE AND DARK TONAL LEVEL, not facial identity.

CORRECTION 1 — REBUILD THE HEAD FROM THE REAL PHOTOS:
Replace the target's generic face and overly voluminous curly hair with a faithful hand-drawn likeness of the real Jackie Leven in images 1–3. Reconstruct the actual contours and relative distances of his forehead, brow, eyes, nose, cheeks, mouth, jaw and neck. His eyes are relatively small and softly hooded; his eyebrows must not become thick dramatic angular brows. Preserve the reference's individual nose length and rounded tip, characteristic small mouth and lip contours, full lower cheeks, soft chin and heavy neck. Match the actual slightly receding hairline and swept wavy hair masses of the photographs; avoid the target's inflated mane. Do not make him younger, thinner, more conventionally handsome, sternly chiseled or generically rugged. No beard or mustache.
Keep the target's general three-quarter head direction toward the viewer's left; a subtly lowered chin and relaxed lowered eyelids are allowed to recover the likeness evident in the photos. He appears absorbed in a quiet pause, not theatrically brooding. The head must be drawn anew from the original photographs, not just the old face covered with more texture.

CORRECTION 2 — MUCH LESS DETAIL, MATCH IMAGE 5:
Use a small number of large, calm, flat gray ink shapes with rough dry-brush boundaries. Simplify the face to roughly 8–12 broad connected light and shadow planes, with only the indispensable accurate feature marks. REMOVE the target's all-over tiny marks, dense hair strands, mottled skin, crackled plaster/oil-paint texture, fine folds and instrument detailing. Broad face planes should be quiet and mostly untextured like the approved image 5. Texture belongs to occasional broken OUTER edges, not a granular veil across everything.
Hair: 5–7 broad dark brush masses and a few restrained gray accents, no individual curls or strands everywhere.
Clothing: a plain dark open-neck shirt, almost a single shadow mass with a few broad strokes.
Guitar: only a broken outer curve, dark soundhole and a minimal suggestion of neck/string direction. Omit the detailed fret grid, rosette, shiny hardware, wood texture and fine parallel strings. Let most of the instrument dissolve into the background.
Hand: relaxed over the upper guitar body as in image 4, normal human proportions and correct fingers, rendered in a handful of broad shapes with almost no knuckle detail; secondary to the face.

Preserve the approved new seated composition and body language of image 4, including the diagonal guitar and resting forearm. Keep his substantial build. Do not reconstruct any photograph's scene. No microphone, stage gear, lanyard, badges, shirt patches, companions or venue.

Palette and background: subdued graphite/slate grays on solid anthracite #0d0f12, matching image 5's WATERMARK-LIKE restraint. Broad light planes around #60676a, midtones #444b50, dark edge accents #30373c; small face accents may reach #73797b. No white face, glow, bright guitar or bright shirt. Keep eyes, nostrils and mouth naturally dark inside lighter planes, no inversion. Outer silhouette and image edges organically disappear into plain #0d0f12. No paper rectangle, border, ornamental halo, lettering, signature, logo or watermark text.
Priority order: accurate likeness to the ORIGINAL photographs; sparse large-form abstraction; approved dark tonal level; existing guitar composition.

steps.title: Flächen und Details reduzieren
steps.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Its newly corrected facial likeness and composition must remain exactly intact.
Image 2 is the approved tonal and stylistic reference of the series, NOT a face reference.
Image 3 is the original 2006 photo of Jackie Leven, included only to protect likeness. Keep image 1's composition, not the photo composition.

ONE CHANGE ONLY: radically simplify the mark-making of image 1 into a sparse FLAT INK PORTRAIT. Preserve its exact facial contours and feature positions, head angle, downcast gaze, mouth, hair silhouette, full cheeks, chin, neck, seated body, resting hand, and diagonal guitar. Do not change the person or pose.

Remove at least 90 percent of all small texture marks. There must be NO tiny mosaic facets, no crackled paint, no plaster texture, no photographic grain, no engraved lines or individually described hair strands. In particular forehead, cheek and hand must become broad UNTEXTURED matte shapes. Render the face in ONLY FOUR flat values: anthracite, deep charcoal, dark slate and restrained mid-gray, with just a few carefully shaped boundaries. The large forehead highlight is ONE coherent quiet shape. The cheek is TWO or THREE coherent quiet shapes. Keep the exact distinctive eyes, nose and mouth with economical accurate marks. Abstraction changes the rendering, not anatomy.

Hair becomes 4–6 big connected dark masses with a handful of broad gray strokes. Shirt becomes one almost black mass with only THREE or FOUR broken broad accents. Hand becomes one flat mid-gray shape with economical dark finger divisions, preserving correct anatomy. Guitar becomes mostly negative space, with only THREE short disconnected curve strokes and a hint of its neck direction. Delete all the fret grid, rosette detailing and almost all strings. Far edges of guitar and clothes disappear completely into the background.

Brush character exists only along a few larger broken contour edges. It must look like confidently reduced ink on dark paper, NOT a detailed oil portrait with a filter. Compare against image 2 and simplify even a little further to compensate for the extra body and instrument.

Maintain the selected low-key gray tonal range on EXACT #0d0f12 anthracite, no increase in brightness. No pure white, no glow, no bright skin. Preserve the exact vertical 4:5 framing and dark margins. No text, signature, frame, props or new elements.
